name: bm-e3-closed-3d-lumenoid
title: Closed 3D lumenoid morphogenesis
claim: A closed 3D lumenoid runs over the Tyssue engine: 78 cells enclose a single lumen, per-cell volumes emerge finite and positive (0.50-3.43), and a basal surface (78 faces, area 202.5) is exposed as the basement-membrane coupling shell with a readable enclosed lumen volume (261.7). The lumen-pressure trajectory and the explicit BM attachment / curvature-dependent shape are the next readouts, not yet dynamic results.
experiment: Build the closed_lumenoid composite (a closed curved Monolayer shell over the vivarium-tyssue engine, its outer basal surface the BM-coupling patch, with a lumen volume/pressure constraint) and step the EulerSolver. Reconstruct the mesh counts (cells, faces, vertices), read every per-cell area and volume off cell_df, read the shell extent off the vertices, and read the lumen volume, lumen pressure and basal BM surface off the engine settings. Confirm the geometry stays finite and positive across several Euler steps (dt 0.01). This is a qualitative morphogenesis check -- that a closed, lumen-enclosing shell resolves with well-posed per-cell geometry and an exposed BM surface -- not yet a lumen-growth trajectory.
result: The closed lumenoid resolves and relaxes deterministically. The shell carries 78 cells, 606 faces and 298 vertices, closed in 3D (vertices span roughly +/-4.7 in x and y and -4.90 to +4.74 in z -- a closed shell centred near the origin, measured extent wider than the +/-4.3 of the earlier reconstruction). Per-cell basal area ranges 3.90-15.65 and per-cell volume 0.50-3.43, all finite and positive. The lumen is readable off the engine: enclosed lumen volume 261.69 (at its preferred volume, so lumen pressure is 0.0 at rest), and the basal BM-coupling surface is 78 faces with total area 202.47. Stepping the EulerSolver five times (dt 0.01) keeps per-cell area and volume finite and positive -- no NaN or blow-up. Because the lumen starts at its preferred volume, the pressure trajectory (pressure departing from zero as the lumen fills or drains) and the explicit BM attachment / curvature-dependent cell-shape predictions are the next readouts, flagged as followups.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: A closed lumen-enclosing shell resolves over the tyssue engine with finite per-cell volumes and an exposed basal BM surface, so the full morphogenesis target is instantiated. Advancing to the curvature-dependent lumen-growth claim additionally requires the lumen-pressure trajectory and the explicit BM attachment, which are flagged as followups.

question: How do lumen pressure/volume and a basement-membrane shell set cell shape and curvature- dependent growth in a closed 3D lumenoid?

purpose.question: How do lumen pressure/volume and a basement-membrane shell set cell shape and curvature- dependent growth in a closed 3D lumenoid?
purpose.mechanism: A closed curved Tyssue epithelium encloses a lumen with a volume/pressure constraint (pressure = elasticity x (volume - preferred volume)) and exposes its outer basal surface as the shell the basement membrane attaches to. A slowly-relaxing BM and a growing lumen are intended to drive curvature-dependent cell shapes -- the new morphogenesis prediction beyond the flat-substrate paper.
purpose.expected_outcome: A closed shell resolves with finite per-cell volumes and a readable enclosed lumen and basal BM surface, establishing the morphogenesis substrate; lumen growth and curvature-dependent cell shape should later depend on BM relaxation once the pressure trajectory and explicit BM attachment are wired.

key_assumptions: The epithelium is a closed curved shell: 78 cells enclose a single lumen, and the outer basal surface is the basement-membrane coupling patch.

The lumen carries a volume/pressure constraint: lumen_pressure = lumen_elasticity x (lumen_vol - lumen_prefered_vol); at initialization the lumen sits at its preferred volume, so pressure is 0.0 at rest.
The BM is treated first as an effective basal surface (78 faces, area 202.47); a collagen patch resolved at the molecular scale (LAMMPS) comes later and is not wired here.
The lumen-pressure trajectory (pressure departing from zero as the lumen fills/drains) is a dynamic readout not yet exercised -- the shell is reported at its rest configuration.
Reduced units throughout; qualitative scope -- this study establishes that a closed lumen-enclosing shell runs with well-posed geometry, not the curvature-dependent growth prediction.

meeting_alignment_2026_10_20.note: Clarify scope: start from an ALREADY CLOSED, formed lumen. Do NOT imply lumen nucleation/lifting is being simulated. Geometry class computes enclosed volume; model-side energy/pressure creates mechanics. Osmotic water-pumping is a LATER extension after passive lumen elasticity.

baseline.name: bm-e3-closed-3d-lumenoid
baseline.note: A closed epithelial shell of 78 cells enclosing a lumen, with the basement membrane as its outer basal surface. The model carries a lumen volume and pressure, and it exposes that basal surface as the membrane the collagen network attaches to. The membrane is treated first as an effective material; a collagen patch resolved at the molecular scale comes later. The lumen-pressure trajectory and the explicit BM attachment are the next readouts.

robustness.note: Deterministic single configuration (one composite, no stochasticity, no parameter variation): the closed-shell geometry is fixed, so a single relaxation run at the lumen's rest volume is the whole evidence. Replication across lumen-pressure / BM-relaxation settings is a gap -- the lumen-growth trajectory is a documented followup.

falsifiability: The claim would be overturned if the closed lumenoid failed to resolve over the tyssue engine, if the cell or face count were zero (an open, non-enclosing mesh), if any per-cell volume were non-finite or non-positive after relaxation, or if stepping the EulerSolver produced a NaN or blow-up. Any of these would show the closed lumen-enclosing shell does not yield well-posed geometry. The contracts in tests/test_tyssue_composites.py (test_closed_lumenoid_runs) would fail in that case.

limitations: Qualitative morphogenesis check only: the study confirms a closed lumen-enclosing shell resolves with finite per-cell volumes and an exposed BM surface, not that lumen growth or curvature set cell shape.

The lumen starts at its preferred volume, so lumen pressure is 0.0 at rest; the pressure trajectory (pressure departing from zero as the lumen fills/drains) is NOT exercised -- it is the next dynamic readout.
The BM is an effective basal surface only (78 faces, area 202.47); the explicit collagen/LAMMPS attachment and the reduced-order-vs-resolved BM consistency check are not wired.
The measured shell extent (roughly +/-4.7 in x/y, -4.90 to +4.74 in z) is wider than the +/-4.3 of the earlier reconstruction -- reported here from the live run.
Single deterministic configuration (no parameter sweep, n_replicates = 1); reduced units, no micron calibration.

config.title: Lumen/BM state is static at rest -- no lumen-filling drive wired (hypothesis)
config.caption: GAP NAMED (hypothesis for a panel not yet producible), real 12-step EulerSolver run, reduced units. The lumen volume (261.7), lumen pressure (0.0) and basal BM-shell surface area (202.5) are FLAT across the run: the shell sits at rest equilibrium and NO lumen-filling drive is wired -- there is no LumenElasticity effector in the force balance and no lumen-volume target ramp, so the lumen is a geometry diagnostic, not a driven degree of freedom. A dynamic lumen-filling / BM-regulated morphogenesis panel is therefore NOT producible from this composite; shown honestly as flat with the gap named.

report.title: E3 -- closed 3D lumenoid (shell runs, lumen readable)
report.verdict: A closed 3D lumenoid resolves over the vivarium-tyssue engine: 78 cells enclose a single lumen (readable volume 261.69, pressure 0.0 at its preferred volume), per-cell volumes emerge finite and positive (0.50-3.43), and a basal surface of 78 faces (area 202.47) is exposed as the basement-membrane coupling shell. The shell is closed in 3D and numerically stable across 5 Euler steps. This instantiates the full morphogenesis target. It is a qualitative rest-state check: the lumen-pressure trajectory and the explicit BM attachment / curvature-dependent cell shape are the next readouts, not yet dynamic results.
report.main_insight: A closed, lumen-enclosing epithelial shell with a readable lumen volume/pressure and an exposed basal BM surface runs over the tyssue engine with well-posed per-cell geometry -- the morphogenesis substrate (cells + lumen + BM shell) exists and is numerically stable.
report.caveat: The lumen sits at its preferred volume (pressure 0.0), and the BM is an effective surface with no explicit attachment, so lumen growth and curvature-dependent shape are not yet tested -- this is a shell-runs result, not a morphogenesis trajectory.

findings.statement: The closed lumenoid resolves over the tyssue engine: 78 cells, 606 faces and 298 vertices form a closed 3D shell (extent roughly +/-4.7 in x/y, -4.90 to +4.74 in z) enclosing a single lumen of volume 261.69; per-cell volumes (0.4961-3.4257) and areas (3.9018-15.6489) emerge finite and positive, and a basal surface of 78 faces (area 202.47) is exposed as the BM-coupling shell.

followup_proposals.title: Drive the lumen and read the pressure/volume trajectory + explicit BM attachment
followup_proposals.motivation: The shell resolves at the lumen's rest volume (pressure 0.0) with an effective (unattached) BM surface, so curvature-dependent lumen growth and cell shape cannot yet be tested. Force the lumen volume (or add influx), record the lumen-pressure/volume trajectory, attach the explicit BM shell, and measure curvature-dependent cell shape against BM relaxation.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: A growing lumen raising pressure against a slowly-relaxing BM shell should produce curvature-dependent cell shapes -- the morphogenesis prediction beyond the flat-substrate paper.

resolved_uncertainties: A closed lumen-enclosing epithelial shell (78 cells + lumen + basal BM surface) resolves over the tyssue engine with finite per-cell volumes.
The lumen volume (261.69), pressure (0.0 at rest) and basal BM surface (78 faces, 202.47) are readable off the engine.
The closed shell is numerically stable over short EulerSolver integration.
remaining_uncertainties: The lumen-pressure/volume trajectory as the lumen grows.
Curvature-dependent cell shape and its dependence on BM relaxation.
The explicit (attached) BM shell vs the effective surface used here.

regression_compatibility.basis: The closed_lumenoid composite is registered and steps cleanly over the vivarium-tyssue engine; the behavior-test contracts (test_closed_lumenoid_runs) pass.

biological_validation.basis: A closed lumen-enclosing shell with finite per-cell volumes and a readable lumen/BM exists, but the lumen-growth trajectory and curvature-dependent cell-shape prediction are not yet exercised, so no morphogenesis claim is validated or refuted here.

explanatory_gain.basis: Instantiating a closed 3D epithelial shell that encloses a readable lumen and exposes a basal BM-coupling surface is a genuine step beyond the flat-substrate models (R1/R4/R5), even before the lumen-growth and curvature predictions are wired.

expert_questions: The lumen starts at its preferred volume (pressure 0.0). Should the canonical E3 run instead drive the lumen off rest (influx or a volume ramp) so the pressure/volume trajectory is part of the evidence?
Is the effective basal BM surface (78 faces, area 202.47) a sufficient coupling shell for the morphogenesis claim, or must the explicit collagen/LAMMPS attachment be wired first?

sources.note: Barrientos et al. cell-shape paper; the closed 3D lumenoid extends the flat-substrate confinement model to a closed curved epithelium with a lumen and a BM shell.
